senses.gloss:
r. 1st cl. (ब्रणति)
To sound; व्रण more properly.

f. (-तिः-ती)
1 A creeper.
2 Expansion.
E.
प्र before तन् to spread, aff. क्तिच्, and प changed to ब; also ब्रतति.

m. (-ध्नः)
1 The root of a tree.
2 The sun.
3 ŚIVA.
4 BRAHMĀ.
5 A son.
6 The body.
E.
बन्ध to bind, aff. नक्, and ब्रध substituted for the root.

f. (-का)
The goddess SARASVATI.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and कन्या the daughter; being born from the head of that deity.

m. (-रिः)
A mountain.
E.
ब्रह्म, and गिरि a hill; the hill of BRAHMĀ.

m. (-कः)
The slayer of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्म, and घातक who kills; also ब्रह्मघातिन् m. (-ती)

m. (-घ्नः)
The slayer of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्म, and घ्न who kills.

m. (-र्य्यः)
The Brahmacarya or Brahmacārī, the religious student: see ब्रह्मचारिन्.
n. (-र्य्यं)
The order or condition of the religious student.
E.
ब्रह्म the Veda, and चर्य्य observance.

n. (-नं)
Incontinence.
E.
ब्रह्मचर्य्य, and स्खलन deviating from.

m. (-री)
The Brahmacārī or religious student; the young Brahman, from the time of his investiture with the cord, to the period of his becoming a householder: it is also applied to a person, who continues with his spiritual teacher, through life, studying the Vedas, and observing the duties of the student; it is also given as a title to Paṇḍitas learned in the Vedas; to a class of ascetics; by the Tantras, it is assigned to persons whose chief virtue is the observance of continence; and it is assumed by many religious vagabonds.
f. (-रिणी)
A woman leading a life of continence.
E.
ब्रह्म the Veda, and चर to go or follow, aff. णिनि.

n. (-न्म)
Second or spiritual birth, investiture.
E.
ब्रह्म the Vedas, and जन्मन् birth.

m. (-वी)
An impure Brahman, one who converts his religious duties into a trade, and performs sacrifice, teaches the Veda, &c. for hire.
E.
ब्रह्मन् an officiating priest, and जीविन् who gets a living.

m. (-ज्ञः)
A sage, one who has spiritual wisdom.
E.
ब्रह्म, and ज्ञ who knows.

n. (-नं)
Spiritual wisdom.
E.
ब्रह्म, and ज्ञान knowledge.

mfn. (-ण्यः-ण्या-ण्यं)
Relating to or connected with BRAHMĀ, or a Brahman.
m. (-ण्यः)
1 The mulberry tree, (Morus Indica.)
2 The planet SATURN.
E.
ब्रह्मन्, and यत् aff.

m. (-ण्यः)
The planet SATURN.
n. (-ण्यं)
1 An assembly of Brahmans.
2 The state, quality, or business of a Brahman, Brahmanhood.
E.
ब्रह्मन्, and यञ् aff., or बाह्मण, and यत् aff.

n. (-त्त्वं)
The true knowledge of Supreme Spirit.
E.
ब्रह्म, and तत्त्व truth.

n. (-त्वं)
1 Identification with BRAHMĀ or GOD.
2 Godhead.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMA, त्व aff. of the abstract; also with तल् aff. ब्रह्मता, or with भूय added ब्रह्मभूय n. (-यं.)

m. (-दः)
A spiritual teacher.
E.
ब्रह्म the Veda or holy knowledge, and द who gives; also ब्रह्मदातृ ब्रह्मदायिन्, &c.

m. (-ण्डः)
1 A plant: see ब्रह्मयष्टि.
2 A curse, an anathema.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and दण्ड a stick.

m. (-त्तः)
One of the sovereigns of the race of Ikṣvāku, enumerated by the Jains.
E.
ब्रह्म by or to BRAHMĀ, दत्त given.

f. (-र्भा)
A plant, (Ligusticum ajwaen, Rox.)
E.
ब्रह्म, and दर्भा sacrificial grass.

n. (-नं)
Instruction in the Vedas.
E.
ब्रह्म, and दान gift; also ब्रह्मदायः.

m. (-रुः)
The mulberry, (Morus Indica.)
E.
ब्रह्म, and दारु wood.

mfn. (-द्विट्)
Hostile to Brahmans, &c.
E.
ब्रह्म, and द्विष् a foe.

m. (-ह्या)
1 BRAHMĀ, the first deity of the Hindu triad, and the operative creator of the world.
2 A Brahman.
3 The superintending or presiding priest at a sacrifice.
4 One of the astronomical Yogas.
5 One of the principal servants of the Jinas.
n. (-ह्म)
1 The divine cause, and essence of the world, from which all created things are supposed to emanate, and to which they return; the unknown God.
2 The practice of austere devotion.
3 The Vedas or scripture.
4 Holy knowledge.
E.
वृह to increase, (mankind,) aff. मनिन् and the initial letter changed to ब.

m. (-भः)
VIṢṆU.
E.
ब्रह्मन् BRAHMĀ, and नाभि the navel; BRAHMĀ having arisen to create the world, in a lotus, which sprang from the navel of VIṢṆU.

n. (-णं)
Absorption into or identification with the Supreme.
E.
ब्रह्म, and निर्व्वाण final absorption.

n. (-दं)
The place or nature of spiritual being.
2 The station or rank of a Brahman or of BRAHMĀ.
E.
ब्रह्म, and पद place.

m. (-पः)
The Palāśa tree, (Butea frondosa.)
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and पादप a tree.

m. (-त्त्रः)
1 A sort of poison.
2 The Brahmaputra or Burampooter river.
3 A place of pilgrimage, probably the source of the stream.
f. (-त्त्री)
1 The Sarasvatī river.
2 The goddess SARASVATĪ.
E.
ब्रह्मन् BRAHMĀ, and पुत्त्र offspring.

f. (-री)
The capital of BRAHMĀ on the mountain Kailāsa.
E.
ब्रह्मन्, and पुरी the city.

m. (-न्धुः)
1 The epithet or appellative of a Brahman.
2 A term of abuse.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and बन्धु a friend.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Become as or one with the Supreme or with spirit.
E.
ब्रह्म, and भूत become.

f. (-तिः)
Twilight.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and भूति being.

n. (-यं)
Identification with BRAHMĀ.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and भूय being.

mfn. (-यः-यी-यं)
Consisting of or identified with spirit.
2 Belonging to or fit for a Brahman, &c.
E.
ब्रह्म, and मयट् aff.

m. (-भृत्)
ŚIVA.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, मूर्द्धन् the forehead, and भृत् who has: having in a dispute cut off one of BRAHMĀ'S heads.

m. (-ज्ञः)
The study of the Vedas.
E.
ब्रह्म a Veda or the Supreme Being, and यज्ञ sacrifice.

f. (-ष्टिः)
A plant, (Ligusticum ajwaen, Rox.)
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and यष्टि a stick; also with कन् added in the fem. form, ब्रह्मंयष्टिका, or with ङीप् added ब्रह्मयष्टी.

m. (-गः)
Cultivation of spiritual knowledge.
E.
ब्रह्म, and योग addition to.

m. (-निः)
A particular mountain.
E.
ब्रह्म, and योनि place of production.

m. (-सः)
A demon or fiend of the Brahminical class.
E.
ब्रह्म, and राक्षस a goblin.

m. (-त्रिः)
1 A name of YĀJÑAVALKYA, a saint and legislator.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, रा to give, ष्ट्रिन् aff.; conferring the knowledge of BRAHMĀ upon JANAKA in return for his bounty.
2 A night of BRAHMĀ, equal to a thousand divine ages.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and रात्रि night.

f. (-तिः)
Brass.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and रीति calx.

m. (-र्षिः)
A divine saint, a Ṛṣi of a particular class, including VAŚIṢṬHA, &c.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and ऋषि a saint; the saints of this class are supposed to be of the Brahminical order.

m. (-शः)
A part of India, including the four countries of Kuru-kṣetra, Matsya, Pañcāla, and Śūrasena or Mathurā.
E.
ब्रह्मर्षि a Ṛṣi, देश country.

m. (-कः)
A division of the universe, the supposed eternal residence of the spirits of the pious.
E.
ब्रह्मन् BRAHMĀ, and लोक a world.

n. (-द्यं)
Knowledge or declaration of BRAHMĀ, the knowledge of the universal permeation of one spirit, as taught by the Vedānta system of philosophy.
E.
BRAHMĀ or the spiritual deity, वद to speak or declare, aff. क्यप्; also with the aff. यत्, and the semivowel changed, ब्रह्मोद्य n. (-द्यं.)

n. (-र्च्चः)
The power or sanctity of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्म, and वर्च्चस् splendour.

n. (-सं)
1 Holiness, resulting from the study and observance of the Vedas.
2 The sanctity or superhuman power of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्म the Vedas, and वर्च्चस् splendour, aff. अच्.

mfn. (-स्वी-स्विनी-स्वि)
1 Endowed with sanctity, pure, pious.
2 Having Brahmanical power or virtue.
E.
ब्रह्मवर्च्चस्, and विनि aff.

m. (-र्त्तः)
A district of western India; also ब्रह्मावर्त्त.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and वृत to abide, aff. अच्.

m. (-र्त्तं)
The country to the north-west of Dehli, lying between the rivers Sarasvatī, and Dṛṣadvatī.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and आवर्त्त abode.

n. (-नं)
Copper.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and वर्द्धन increasing, favouring; being highly proper for utensils of worship, &c.

m. (-दः)
1 Citing the Vedas.
2 Declaring or teaching spiritual knowledge.
E.
ब्रह्म scripture. and वाद speaking.

m. (-दी)
1 A follower of the Vedānta system of philosophy, one who maintains all things are spirit.
2 A defender or expounder of the Veda.
E.
ब्रह्म the Veda or BRAHMĀ, GOD, and वादिन् who recites.

m. (-वित् or विद्)
A sage, one who knows the nature of the Supreme Spirit.
E.
ब्रह्म, and विद् who knows.

f. (-द्या)
Knowledge of spirit.
E.
ब्रह्म, and विद्या science.

m. (-न्दुः)
Saliva sputtered out in reading the Vedas.
E.
ब्रह्म scripture, and विन्दु a drop.

f. (-न्दा)
The capital of BRAHMĀ.
E.
ब्रह्मन्, and वृन्द heap, assemblage.

m. (-दः)
1 Knowledge of BRAHMĀ, monotheism.
2 Knowledge of the Vedas.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and वेद knowing.

m. (-क्षः)
1 The Palāśa tree, (Butea frondosa.)
2 The glomerous fig tree.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and वृक्ष a tree.

f. (-दिः)
A country: see ब्रह्मावर्त्त.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and वेदि a country.

mfn. (-दी-दिनी-दि)
Knowing or acquainted with the Vedas, with spiritual knowledge, &c.
E.
ब्रह्म, and वेदिन् who knows.

m. (-ल्यः)
A tree, (Mimosa Arabica.)
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and शल्य a stake.

n. (-नं)
An edict or grant, &c. addressed to Brahmans.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and शासन governing or an edict, &c.

n. (-त्रं)
1 Study and teaching of the Vedas.
2 The constant study of them.
E.
ब्रह्म, and सत्र sacrifice.

m. (-र्पः)
A sort of snake.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and सर्प a snake.

mfn. (-वः-वा-वं)
Born or produced from BRAHMĀ.
m. (-वः)
The second of the persons called Vāsudevas or Kṛṣṇas by the Jains.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and सम्भव offspring.

n. (-ज्यं)
Identification with BRAHMĀ.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and सायुज्य intimate union.

f. (-ता)
Equality with BRAHMĀ.
E.
ब्रह्म, and सार्ष्टिता sameness.

f. (-ला)
A plant, an infusion of which is to be drank in expiation of having any thing touched by a dog, cat, &c.
E.
ब्रह्म, and सुवर्च्चला linseed.

m. (-सूः)
1 ANIRUDDHA, the son of KĀMA.
2 KĀMADEVA.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and सू the son.

n. (-त्रं)
1 The sacrificial or Brahmanical thread.
2 An aphorism of the Vedānta philosophy.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, and सूत्र thread.

m. (नुः)
A sovereign, according to the Jains, of the race of Ikṣvāku.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and सूनु son.

mfn. (-पः-पा-पं)
Of the nature of spirit, of the same essence as the Godhead.
E.
ब्रह्म, and स्वरूप nature.

f. (-त्या)
1 Brahmanicide, killing a Brahman.
2 Any crime equally heinous.
E.
ब्रह्म, and हत्या killing.

m. (-हा)
The murderer or slayer of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्मन्, and हन who kills.

n. (-तं)
The performance of hospitality, &c., that one of the great sacraments which consists in the veneration of mankind.
E.
ब्रह्म a Brahman, हुत worshipped; being the most worthy of respect, &c.

m. (-रः)
The sacred and mysterious name of the deity.
E.
ब्रह्म GOD, अक्षर a letter, the Oṃkāra.

m. (-भूः)
A horse.

m. (-लिः)
1 Joining both hands together, whilst reading the Vedas, either as an act of humility or to mark the accentuation of the Sāma Veda.
2 Paying obeisance to the spiritual preceptor at the beginning or end of a lecture.
E.
ब्रह्म the Vedas, and अञ्जलि the hands joined.

f. (-णी)
1 The female energy of BRAHMĀ.
2 A sort of perfume, commonly Reṇukā.
E.
ब्रह्मन् BRAHMĀ, fem. aff. ङीप्.

m. (-ण्डः)
1 The globe, the world.
2 One of the Purāṇas.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and अण्ड an egg, to which it is compared; in creation there are said to have been innumerable Brahmāṇḍas.

n. (-नं)
Perusal of the Vedas.
E.
ब्रह्म, and अधिगमन going through; also ब्रह्मधिगम.

mfn. (-कः-की-कं)
Relating or contributing to a course of sacred study.
E.
ब्रह्माधिगम, and ठञ् aff.

m. (-सः)
Study or repetition of scripture.
E.
ब्रह्न, and अभ्यास exercise.

n. (-म्भः)
Cow's urine.
E.
ब्रह्मन् a Brahman, and अम्भस् water.

n. (-ण्यं)
A place where the Vedas are read and explained.
E.
ब्रह्म the Veda, and अरण्य a wood.

n. (-नं)
A posture suited to devout and religious meditation.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, and आसन sitting.

n. (-स्वं)
1 The BRAHMĀ weapon, a fabulous weapon originally from BRAHMĀ.
2 The imprecation of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्म, and अस्व a weapon.

f. (-तिः)
An oblation of ghee.
E.
ब्रह्म the Veda, and आहुति an offering.

f. (-ह्मी)
1 A sort of fish, commonly Pancal, (Macrognathus Pancalus, HAM.)
2 A plant, (Siphonanthus Indica.)
E.
वृह to grow or increase, affs. मनिन and ङीप्^1; also ब्रह्मी.
[1] Correction submitted by Jim Funderburk on 20161212. Reference: https://github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/CORRECTIONS/issues/323, batches 309-312. note: missing virAma.

f. (-ता)
Neglecting or forgetting the Veda.
E.
ब्रह्म, and उज्झता abandonment.

n. (-द्यं)
Reciting or explaining the Vedas.
E.
ब्रह्म, and वद to speak, aff. क्यप्.

n. (-नं)
Boiled rice distributed to priests at a sacrifice.
E.
ब्रह्मन् a Brahman, and ओदन boiled rice.

mfn. (-ह्मः-ह्मी-ह्मं)
Relating or belonging to BRAHMĀ, the Vedas, &c.
n. (-ह्मं)
1 The part of the hand under the root of the thumb.
2 A mode of marriage, the presentation of the bride elegantly adorned, by the father, to the bridegroom whom he has invited.
m. (-ह्मः)
NĀRADA the sage, and son of BRAHMĀ.
f. (-ह्मी)
1 One of the eight divine mothers of created beings, or the personified energies of the gods; the Śakti or energy of BRAHMĀ.
2 The goddess of speech SARASVATĪ.
3 The moon plant, (Asclepias acida.)
4 A sort of potherb, (Ruta graveolens.)
5 A shrub, (Siphonanthus Indica.)
6 A sort of fish.
7 The asterism Rohiṇī.
8 A she frog.
9 A yellow coloured ant.
10 The wife of a Brahman.
E.
ब्रह्म BRAHMĀ, &c. अण् aff.

m. (-णः)
A man of the first Hindu tribe, a Brahman.
n. (-णं)
1 An assemblage of Brahmans, a council, a conclave.
2 A portion of the Vedas, that which comprises the precepts that inculcate religious duties, the maxims which explain those precepts, and the arguments which relate to theology; it is, however, now often blended with other portions.
f. (-णी)
1 The wife of a Brahman, or a woman of the Brahmanical tribe.
2 A wasp.
3 A small ant.
4 A potherb, (Ruta graveolens.)
5 A shrub, (Siphonanthus Indica.)
6 A sort of grass, (Trigonella corniculata.)
E.
ब्रह्मन् the Veda, &c. अण् aff., and the final syllable of the original word retained.

m. (-लः)
An outcaste Brahman, one who is attended by a wife of another caste, or the son of a Śūdra by a Brahman female.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and चाण्डाल an outcaste.

f. (-तिः)
The Brahmanical tribe or caste.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and जाति tribe.

mfn. (-यः-या-यं)
Belonging to the Brahmanical race.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and जातीय generic.

f. (-का)
The occupation or subsistence of a Brahman.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and जीविका livelihood.

f. (-ता)
Brahmanhood.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and तल् aff.; also with त्व, ब्राह्मणत्वं.

m. (-धः)
Brahmanicide.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and बध killing.

m. (-वः)
A Brahman by birth but not by attention to his duties; one who subsists by avocations properly limited to the other tribes.
E.
ब्राह्मण a Brahman, and ब्रुव who speaks, who calls himself (improperly) a Brahman.

f. (-का)
A shrub, (Siphonanthus Indica.)
E.
ब्राह्मण a Brahman, and यष्टि a staff, aff. कन्.

mfn. (-स्थः-स्था-स्थं)
Belonging to or abiding with a Brahman.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and संस्थ what stays with.

mfn. (-तः-ता-तं)
Suitable to or fit for a Brahman.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and हित proper.

m. (-मः)
Disregarding or disrespecting Brahmans.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and अतिक्रम going over or beyond.

mfn. (-कः-का-कं)
Belonging to, one or with or containing Brahmans, the Brāhmaṇa section of the Vedas, &c.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and आत्मक own.

n. (-नं)
Absence of Brahmanical instruction or guidance.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and अदर्शन not showing or teaching.

f. (-त्तिः)
The protection or preservation of a Brahman.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and अभ्युपपत्ति defence.

m. (-नः)
A Brahman, sprung from learned and holy progenitors.
E.
ब्राह्मण, and फञ् aff.

m. (-मी)
The gallant of a woman of the Brahmanical tribe, or the wife of a Brahman.
E.
ब्राह्मणी a female Brahman, and गामिन् who goes to or with.

f. (-या)
A girl to be wedded by the Brāhma form.
E.
ब्राह्म, and देय to be given.

f. (-ङ्गा)
Silver.

m. (-त्रः)
A day and night of BRAHMĀ, a period of two thousand ages of the gods or two Kalpas of mortals.
E.
ब्राह्मण relating to BRAHMĀ, अहन् a day, and रात्रि a night.

f. (-का)
A shrub, (Siphonanthus Indica.)
E.
ब्राह्मी, and कन् aff.

m. (-त्त्रः)
The son of a woman married according to the Brāhma form.
E.
ब्राह्मी, and पुत्त्र a son.

n. (-ह्म्यं)
1 The worship or veneration of Brahmans, considered as one of the great sacraments.
2 Astonishment.
E.
ब्रह्म, and ष्यञ् aff.

n. (-तं)
Respect shown to guests, especially to Brahmans, hospitality.
E.
ब्राह्म्य, and हुत sacrifice.
